subject: Recap: Acme Logistics performance discovery — latency & burst profile
messages:
From: Jamie Reed <jamie.reed@acme-logistics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Soto <alex.soto@acme-logistics.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme demo follow-up — workload snapshot attached

Monica / Rishi — thanks for the walkthrough today. Jamie here (Acme Ops). Quick recap and a few clarifications from our side — attaching the workload snapshot we pulled from our staging cluster (acme_workload_snapshot.csv).

What we believe matters for sizing:
- Steady-state QPS: ~8–12 QPS across the day (typical traffic).
- Short bursts: large ingestion jobs (customer data imports) cause synchronous request spikes: we observed ~600 QPS sustained for ~90–150 seconds during the last import. These happen roughly 2–3x per day during business hours.
- Average tokens per API request: ~1,200 tokens (prompt + response); 95th token case ~8,000 for some diagnostic queries.
- Streaming: roughly 30% of requests use streaming; average open-stream duration 25–45s.
- Latency expectations: product team desires P95 end-to-end <= 200–300ms for “interactive” paths; we can tolerate higher latency for backend batch jobs.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Given the above, what sizing / model recommendations do you suggest for Hosted vs Dedicated?
2) Can you run a short sizing test against our staging workload (we can provide temporary credentials)?
3) Are there config knobs (KV cache, prefix caching, batching) that could meaningfully reduce tokens/sec or tail latency during bursts?

Next steps we want: mutual action plan and a short proposal so our procurement team has material. We aim to decide by 2027-08-15.

Attachments: acme_workload_snapshot.csv (csv)

—
Jamie Reed
Senior Ops Manager, Acme Logistics
jamie.reed@acme-logistics.com
+1 (415) 555-0142
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Reed <jamie.reed@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme demo follow-up — workload snapshot attached

Jamie — thanks for the clear recap and for sending the snapshot. High-level read and immediate clarifications below. I’ve also attached a short placeholder proposal (redwood_proposal_v1.pdf) so procurement has something to review while we narrow sizing.

Quick read on the numbers you sent:
- Steady QPS 8–12 and 600 QPS short bursts aligns with what we saw in the CSV.
- 1,200 avg tokens / request with ~30% streaming is helpful — streaming changes memory/KV cache behavior, so we’ll call that out in recommendations.

Clarifying asks (so our recommendation is precise):
- During a burst, how many concurrent distinct users/sessions are active (concurrency)? From your notes it sounds like bursts are from automated imports (many parallel requests) vs many end-user sessions — please confirm.
- For streaming flows, are clients doing chunked responses (client pulls every 200ms) or server-sent streaming with long-lived HTTP streams?
- Any hard SLOs other than the P95 guidance? You mentioned 200–300ms — is 200ms the target for go/no-go, or can we scope a phased ramp (e.g., 300ms acceptable for initial rollout and 200ms an objective)?

Preliminary recommendations (to iterate):
- Hosted with autoscale (start) + Dedicated reserve for predictable burst windows OR Dedicated 8 GPU baseline (A100-eq) with autoscale headroom. We will provide cost/latency tradeoffs in the detailed proposal.
- Enable prefix caching for repeated prompt prefixes (likely to shave ~15–30% of tokens served if you have repeated system prompts).
- KV cache sizing: stream sessions increase KV working set; we’ll propose a cache strategy to avoid expensive KV reloads during bursts.

Proposed next steps:
1) Acme provides a 24‑hour telemetry export for one trough and one burst window (CSV or query access) — owner: Jamie (due: 2027-07-03).
2) Redwood runs a 60‑minute profiling run against staging + a 15‑minute peak replay to validate tail; results and a draft sizing plan shared within 5 business days after data receipt — owner: Monica / Rishi (target publish: 2027-07-12).
3) Follow-up call to walk the sizing and procurement items (30–45m) — propose 2027-07-14 or 07-15.

If that plan works I’ll kick off the profiling schedule and send a more detailed internal runbook for the staging creds.

Attachments: redwood_proposal_v1.pdf (proposal stub)

—
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Acme demo follow-up — workload snapshot attached

On Tue, Jun 29, 2027 at 15:05, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> Monica — thanks for the clear recap and for sending the snapshot. High-level read and immediate clarifications below.

Small clarifications from my side:
- Bursts are indeed ingestion jobs (server-side triggered). Concurrency during the 600 QPS window was ~420 concurrent inflight requests (we measure at our LB).
- Streaming is server-sent HTTP chunking; clients keep a connection open and we push tokens as they arrive.
- Nightly maintenance window at 02:00–03:00 PT occasionally reduces baseline by ~40%.
- We require SOC2 evidence and prefer a VPC/private deployment for production (this will likely push us toward Dedicated/Private).
- Procurement timeline: aiming for internal approval by 2027-08-15; budget is not finalized but indicative.

I attached the product requirements doc (acme_requirements.pdf) with some security checkboxes. Happy to provide a short telemetry query if that speeds the profiling.

—
Alex Soto
Platform Lead, Acme Logistics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Reed <jamie.reed@acme-logistics.com>, Alex Soto <alex.soto@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme demo follow-up — workload snapshot attached

Thanks for the details, Alex / Jamie — super helpful. Adding a few technical bullets and an action list from the Redwood side.

Technical notes / quick sizing heuristics:
- If bursts are ~600 QPS with ~420 concurrent inflight, and average tokens/request ~1,200, then raw token ingress at peak is ~720k tokens/sec; with response tokens included you should plan for ~1.0M token/sec headroom during the ~2–3 minute spike.
- For a hosted autoscale path we recommend: baseline pool to cover 12 QPS steady (low cost), with burst headroom via fast scale + pre-warmed burst nodes (or temporary Dedicated credits). For private/dedicated the starting point would be a baseline of 8 A100-eq GPUs with autoscale to +4 GPUs for peak windows — we will provide more precise GPU count after profiling.
- Streaming impacts: P95 latency target should be split: streaming P95 <= 220ms, non-streaming P95 <= 180ms (these are achievable with the right batching / KV cache sizing and model variant choices).
- Caching & batching: enabling prefix cache plus a modest batching window (30–50ms) should reduce per-token cost and improve throughput without materially harming tail latency for interactive flows.

Action items (owners & dates):
- Jamie: share 24‑hour telemetry with a representative peak window (CSV or DB query) — due 2027-07-03.
- Monica / Rishi: run profiling (60m profile + 15m peak replay) after telemetry received — deliverables: latency/QPS/p50/p95/p99 and KV hit rates — target 2027-07-12.
- Marissa: run a 30m hosted proof-of-load on our staging fleet (simulated peak) and produce a short writeup with recommended GPU counts and estimated monthly cost — target 2027-07-16.
- Monica: schedule the follow-up 45m sizing + procurement call (proposed 2027-07-14) — pending availability.

Let us know if Acme wants us to run the profiling in their VPC (we can, with an NDA and temporary keys) or if you prefer a staged hosted run first.

Attachments referenced: acme_requirements.pdf, acme_workload_snapshot.csv, redwood_proposal_v1.pdf

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
